core_obligations: Verify the weak Serre axioms for A_X (proof lines 7376-7401): for a map phi : F -> G in A_X the kernel and cokernel of epsilon_{X,*}phi lie in A'_X because that is a weak Serre subcategory, and applying epsilon_X^{-1} produces the exact sequence exhibiting Ker phi and Coker phi as objects of A_X.

Verify closedness under extensions (proof lines 7402-7411): a short exact sequence in Ab(C_tau/X) whose outer terms lie in A_X becomes, after applying epsilon_{X,*}, a short exact sequence of objects of A'_X, and applying epsilon_X^{-1} returns the middle term, giving the extension closure.

Conclude the weak Serre property (proof lines 7413-7416), so that D^+_{A_X} makes sense, and then note that epsilon_X^{-1} : A'_X -> A_X is an equivalence and that F' -> R epsilon_{X,*} epsilon_X^{-1} F' is an isomorphism for F' in A'_X because the conditions (V_n) hold for all n by the V-C lemma (proof lines 7417-7421).
Apply the equivalence criterion (proof line 7422) to obtain the asserted equivalence of triangulated categories with quasi-inverse epsilon_X^{-1}.
proof_roadmap: Check the weak Serre axioms for A_X by transporting kernels, cokernels and extensions along epsilon_{X,*} and epsilon_X^{-1}.
Record that epsilon_X^{-1} is an equivalence A'_X -> A_X and that the unit F' -> R epsilon_{X,*} epsilon_X^{-1} F' is an isomorphism by the V-C lemma for all n.
Apply the general equivalence criterion for bounded below derived categories to finish.
difficulty_reason: The lemma is the general cohomological descent statement for the comparison of two topologies: A_X is a weak Serre subcategory and R epsilon_{X,*} : D^+_{A_X} -> D^+_{A'_X} is an equivalence (statement lines 7360-7373). The proof (proof lines 7375-7422) verifies the weak Serre axioms by transporting kernels, cokernels and extensions along epsilon_{X,*} and epsilon_X^{-1}, and then invokes the equivalence criterion for bounded below derived categories, the hypotheses (V_n) for all n having been provided by the V-C lemma. H2: a verification of standard axioms followed by one application of the equivalence criterion.
